outcome: Specific patterns of congenital anomalies (CVS, GIT, genitourinary, musculoskeletal, CNS, respiratory)
cohort: The participants were all cases admitted in the neonatal care unit of the study hospital.
finding: The study found that CVS anomalies were the most common (36.3%), followed by GIT (16.5%), and congenital anomalies were more frequent in males (M:F = 1.5:1).
mod_finding: The frequency of congenital anomalies was higher in vaginal deliveries (2.7%) compared to cesarean born babies (1.58%).
cross-section timing: Data was collected over one year for neonates admitted to the neonatal care unit.
